title: Jeff Bezos announces radically fired at Space Company Blue Origin
text:
By Noa Halff for DailyMail.com
Published: 21:30 GMT, February 13, 2025 | Updated: 21:45 GMT, February 13, 2025
The space of Jeff Bezos’ Space Venture Blue Origin has announced drastic dismissals – axen no less than 1,400 jobs – or 10 percent of his workforce.
In a meeting of 10 minutes on Thursday, CEO Dave Limp delivered the news to employees in the most important hubs of the company in Florida, Texas and Washington.
The shock announcement only comes a few weeks after Blue Origin starts with production on his huge new Glenn Rocket.
“There is no easy way to communicate this,” CEO Dave Limp told the employees at the meeting, who was planned the night before and lasted about 10 minutes. “There is no doubt that we have had many successes in recent months.”
“But having said that, if you look at the base of the company and what we have to achieve for the next three to five years, we just came to the painful conclusion that we were not set up for the kind of success we really wanted,” ” Limp said.
At the end of 2023, Limp was hired by Bezos itself from the Amazon’s Consumer Electronics Division.
Limp said that the last shake-up would help the company scale up new Glenn production and increase the launch frequency.
That would be the key to catch up with the dominant Falcon 9 of SpaceX.

To do that, the company needs a culture that is ‘fast, agile, decisive and very focused on our customer,’ he said as reported by Reuters.
Since taking over, LIMP is the task of streamlining the Blue Origin projects with urgency after years of development delays.
But not everyone is on board.
Two employees revealed to Reuters that it has plummeted under the leadership of Limp.
Some employees are reportedly even looking for other jobs.
In January, the launch of the new Glenn Rocket from Florida marked the company’s first attempt to challenge the dominance of SpaceX in the space industry.
To X after the launch tweeted Limp at the time: ‘We did it! Orbital. Great evening for Team Blue. Continue to the spring and try again on landing. ‘
The new Glenn rocket, powered by a combination of liquid oxygen and methane, is intended to compete with Elon Musk’s SpaceX by offering reliable and cost-effective satellite launches.
The mission of Blue Origin was not only about the trip of the Rocket, but also about testing the company’s booster recovery options.
A Blue Origin New Shepard Rocket is launching one in West Texas north of Van Horn from launch site one

Ten minutes after the launch, it was expected that the first phase of New Glenn would return to Earth, aimed at a precision landing on a sieve harge in the Atlantic Ocean, while the second phase of the rocket continued his journey to a job.
Unfortunately, the company confirmed that this part of the mission failed, with a spokesperson for Blue Origin who admitted: “We have lost the booster.”
In the Payload -Bay van de Raket there was a considerable piece of future of Blue Origin – the blue ring vehicle, a prototype spacecraft designed to be maneuverable in space.
The company plans to sell this vehicle to the US military and commercial customers for satellite service and national security activities.
The successful launch of the spacecraft in a job would be a rare performance for every space company, especially on their inaugural mission.
